requirement:
Each `AgentConfig` variant carries the corresponding settings from
`trust_but_verify::agent`. Serde uses the `backend` field to select `bedrock`,
`openai`, or `ollama` and reads the settings from the same object.

Choose [`BedrockConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.BedrockConfig),
[`OpenAiConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OpenAiConfig), or
[`OllamaConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OllamaConfig) for the selected backend.
With settings omitted, OpenAI uses `gpt-6.1-sol`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`,
and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Ollama defaults to `http://localhost:11434`.

All three backend constructors start with an empty `options` map. Calling
`option(key, value)` inserts one inference setting. Calling it again with the
same key replaces its value and preserves the other settings. An `OptionValue` is
a `String`, `Boolean`, `Integer(i64)`, `Float(f64)`, `Array`, or `Map`. Arrays hold
option values and maps associate strings with option values. These serialize as
the corresponding untagged values. Backend calls reject nonfinite floats,
including those nested in an array or map.

`BedrockCredentials` contains `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key`, both
`SecretString`, and an optional `session_token` of the same type. Construct a
`SecretString` from `String` or `&str`. `expose_secret()` borrows its value.
Serialization preserves the string, while `Debug` prints `<redacted>`.
rationale:
I judged the marked tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs` adequate for `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.agent_config.settings`. I did not request implementation source. Each obligation maps to tests as follows.

- **Variants carry settings, and `backend` selects the variant.**
  - `all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials` deserializes `bedrock`, `openai` and `ollama` objects with the settings in the same object.
  - It asserts that serializing gives back the identical JSON and that a round trip through a string gives an equal `AgentConfig`.
  - `openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults` checks that `{"backend":"openai"}` equals `AgentConfig::OpenAi(OpenAiConfig::new())`.
  - `configuration_debug_hides_credentials` checks that an unknown field is rejected.
- **OpenAI defaults.**
  - `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` asserts the default model `gpt-6.1-sol` and endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
  - `openai_uses_the_default_credential_variable` re-runs itself in a child process with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set. There `OpenAiConfig::new().resolved_api_key()` returns the variable's value, which covers the default variable name.
- **Ollama default endpoint.** `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` asserts `http://localhost:11434`.
- **Empty `options` at construction.** In `backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields`, all three constructors serialize without any `options` entry.
- **`option(key, value)` inserts and replaces.** The same test sets `a=1`, then `b=true`, then `a=2` on Bedrock, OpenAI and Ollama. Each serializes to `{"a":2,"b":true}`, so the replacement keeps the other setting.
- **`OptionValue` variants and untagged serialization.**
  - `all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials` covers a string, a boolean, an integer, a float, a nested map and an array, and checks they serialize to the same JSON.
  - `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` checks that `1` deserializes to `Integer` and `1.0` to `Float`.
- **Nonfinite floats rejected, including nested ones.** `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` checks that infinity inside a map fails `validate()`. It also checks that NaN inside an array makes `AgentConfig::Ollama(...).options_json()` fail. Both nesting forms are covered.
- **`BedrockCredentials`.**
  - `backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields` covers `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key` without a token. It also covers the optional `session_token` and the Bedrock serialization that includes the credentials.
  - `all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials` round-trips credentials that include a session token.
- **`SecretString`.** `configuration_debug_hides_credentials` covers the following:
  - construction from `&str` and from `String`;
  - `expose_secret()` returning the value;
  - `Debug` printing `<redacted>`;
  - serialization preserving the string;
  - deserialization of a plain string;
  - inequality between different secrets.

I found no uncovered obligation or weak assertion. Two minor omissions do not matter. Negative infinity is not tested separately from positive infinity or NaN. The nonfinite check is not repeated per backend. Neither is a distinct requirement-relevant class.
